skill.description: Build and train AgentDB learning plugins with reinforcement learning templates, CLI workflows, API examples, and training patterns for adaptive AI agents.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, TypeScript examples, JSON examples, and reference links. I confirmed the Bash sections that direct users to run `npx agentdb@latest` because automated execution would run remote npm package code, and confirmed the local SQLite example as a data persistence risk. I found no prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or hidden executable file.

remediation.issue: Bash examples use `npx agentdb@latest` for plugin and MCP operations.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user-confirmation guidance, pin package versions for automated workflows, and recommend running commands in an isolated project.
Document data minimization, retention, cleanup, and sensitive-data handling for local AgentDB learning databases.

content.value_statement: Reinforcement learning agents are hard to scaffold, train, and compare. This skill guides AgentDB plugin creation with CLI steps, API examples, and algorithm choices.
actual_capabilities: Explains nine AgentDB reinforcement learning plugin templates and their best-fit use cases.
Shows CLI workflows for creating, listing, and inspecting AgentDB learning plugins.
Demonstrates AgentDB adapter setup with learning enabled and a local training database.
Describes how to store experiences, train models, and evaluate learned behavior.
Covers advanced patterns such as replay, multi-agent training, and incremental learning.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for convergence, overfitting, and slow training.
limitations: Requires Node.js and AgentDB from the agentic-flow ecosystem.
Assumes users understand basic reinforcement learning concepts.
Examples are instructional and still need production validation and monitoring.
Local training data may contain sensitive information unless users minimize and clean it.

use_cases.title: Prototype an RL Plugin
use_cases.description: Select a learning algorithm and create an AgentDB plugin plan for a new adaptive agent.

use_cases.title: Add Learning to an Agent
use_cases.description: Store agent experiences, train on outcomes, and retrieve similar successful decisions.

use_cases.title: Compare Training Strategies
use_cases.description: Evaluate Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, and advanced learning approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Algorithm
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an AgentDB learning plugin template for my agent. Ask about action space, data availability, safety needs, and evaluation goals.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Plugin Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step plan to scaffold an AgentDB learning plugin for [agent goal]. Include prerequisites, template choice, training data needs, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Training Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AgentDB training workflow for [domain]. Include experience collection, batch size, epochs, evaluation metrics, and troubleshooting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB learning plugin design for multi-agent or federated training. Identify risks, data retention concerns, algorithm tradeoffs, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Choose a template for an agent that learns from past support-ticket resolutions.
output_examples.output: Recommended Decision Transformer. It fits logged experience data, supports offline learning, and avoids unsafe online exploration during early testing.

output_examples.input: Plan a Q-Learning plugin for a navigation task.
output: Template: Q-Learning for a discrete action space.
Training data: state, action, reward, next state, and done flag for each step.
Validation: compare success rate, average reward, and failure cases across episodes.

output_examples.output: Likely causes include oversized batches, repeated full retraining, and missing inference optimization. Suggested fixes include smaller batches, incremental training, and quantized inference.

best_practices: Validate training data and remove sensitive fields before writing to AgentDB.
Pin AgentDB package versions instead of using floating latest in automated workflows.
Start with small offline experiments and compare metrics before enabling incremental training.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-run npx commands from a community skill without user confirmation.
Do not store raw private conversations or credentials in the local learning database.
Do not train continuously without validation, rollback, and resource limits.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan, create, train, and evaluate AgentDB learning plugins for adaptive AI agents.

faq.question: Which algorithms are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, active learning, adversarial training, curriculum learning, federated learning, and multi-task learning.

faq.question: Do I need reinforcement learning experience?
faq.answer: Basic reinforcement learning knowledge is recommended because the examples use states, actions, rewards, training metrics, and evaluation loops.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI commands, but users should confirm and run them intentionally in a controlled project.

faq.question: Where is training data stored?
faq.answer: The examples use a local AgentDB database path. Users should avoid storing sensitive data and define retention rules.
